Christ in All Scripture
KRYST in AWL SKRIP-cher
proper noun
The principle that the whole of Scripture, Old Testament and New, testifies of Christ (Luke 24:27; John 5:39).

Biblical Definition

Christ in all Scripture is the principle, taught by the Lord Jesus Himself, that the whole of the written Word—the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms—testifies of Him, so that He is the substance and center of all the Scriptures. On the road to Emmaus, beginning at Moses and all the prophets, He expounded unto the disciples in all the scriptures the things concerning Himself; and to the gathered eleven He said that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning Him. To the unbelieving He said, Search the scriptures, for in them ye think ye have eternal life, and they are they which testify of me; and, Had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me, for he wrote of me. Thus the promised Seed of Genesis, the Passover lamb, the rock in the wilderness, the suffering Servant of Isaiah, the smitten Shepherd of Zechariah, the Son of man of Daniel, and the King of the Psalms all point to Christ; the Old Testament is the gospel in promise, type, and prophecy, and the New is its fulfillment. The dictionary reads Christ in all Scripture as the unifying key to the Bible: He is the theme of the whole, foreshadowed in the Old and revealed in the New, so that to read the Scriptures rightly is to find Christ in them, from Genesis to Revelation.

Webster 1828 Definition

The principle, taught by Christ Himself, that the whole of Scripture testifies of Him; the Old Testament foreshadows and the New reveals the one theme of the Bible.

Luk 24:44 — "And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me."

Joh 5:39 — "Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me."

Joh 5:46 — "For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me."

Modern Corruption

Higher criticism severs the Old Testament from Christ as merely ancient religion, and a flat moralism reads it for examples only; the Lord teaches that all the Scriptures testify of Him.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Two errors sever Christ from the Scriptures. The first is the higher-critical reading that treats the Old Testament as merely the evolving religion of ancient Israel, with no genuine prophecy and no real foreshadowing of Christ, so that the connections the New Testament draws are dismissed as creative misreadings. The second is a flat moralism that mines the Old Testament only for examples of behavior—be brave like David, be pure like Joseph—and never finds the Christ to whom every story points. Both miss what the Lord Himself taught: the Scriptures testify of Him, and Moses wrote of Him.

The principle to recover is Christ as the unifying theme and substance of the whole Bible. He expounded in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself and declared that the law, the prophets, and the psalms all speak of Him. The promised Seed, the Passover lamb, the bronze serpent, the suffering Servant, the smitten Shepherd, the Son of man, the royal Bridegroom of the Psalms—all foreshadow Him; the Old Testament is the gospel in promise and type, the New its fulfillment. To read the Scriptures rightly is to find Christ in them, for of Him they testify from first to last.
